budget.countFirst: Run git diff --numstat <base>...<branch> and git log --oneline <base>..<branch> before reading any hunk. Three dots for git diff (merge-base form, so the diff holds only the branch's own changes), two for git log (the commit range). Record every file with its line counts, and every commit, in the findings document's budget block. A numstat row of - - is a binary file: list it in budget.binaryFiles by path, count it as 0 lines, and never invent a count for it or drop it.
readOrder: files the issue declares under Files to modify
remaining files by diff size ascending
budget.overBudget: A file not read in full because a cap was reached is listed in budget.countedNotRead with its path and line count. It is never silently dropped: the count is evidence, and a non-empty countedNotRead caps the verdict at warn.

criteria.name: Every hunk maps to an acceptance criterion
criteria.description: Each hunk in the range serves at least one of the issue's acceptance criteria, or is flagged as unrelated work.
criteria.check: For each hunk, name the AC it serves. A hunk serving no AC is a finding: unrelated work landing under this issue's Refs #N misattributes it to the gates that key off that commit set.
criteria.evidence: File, hunk header, and either the AC it maps to or the word 'unrelated' with one line saying what the hunk does instead.

criteria.name: No files outside the declared scope
criteria.description: Every changed file is named by the issue's Files to modify declaration or its Files Changed section.
criteria.check: Compare git diff --name-only <base>...<branch> against the declared paths. A changed file the declaration does not name is a finding. Always-protected paths (framework-config.json, framework-manifest.json, .claude/metadata/**, .gh-pmu.json, CHARTER.md) are findings even when a Files Changed section lists them, because only the authored declaration can license them.
criteria.evidence: The undeclared path and the declaration it is absent from.

criteria.name: Tests present for new behavior
criteria.description: New or changed behavior in the range has a test in the same range that exercises it.
criteria.check: For each source hunk that adds or changes behavior, find a test hunk in the range that asserts it. A behavior with no test in the range is a finding; a non-code artifact (spec, JSON, markdown) needs a contract test declaring it as a subject.
criteria.evidence: The source file and line, and either the test file and test name that covers it or the statement that none was found in the range.

criteria.name: Tests are authentic
criteria.description: Tests in the range verify behavior rather than mirror the implementation or assert trivially.
criteria.check: Judge each test in the range by the framework's /bad-test-review criteria, read from .claude/commands/bad-test-review.md at review time. Do not restate those criteria here; a second definition drifts silently from the first.
criteria.evidence: The test file and test name, the /bad-test-review criterion it fails, and the assertion that shows it.

criteria.name: Charter conventions honored
criteria.description: The change uses the tech stack and follows the conventions the project charter declares.
criteria.check: Read the charter's Tech Stack and any conventions it states. A hunk that introduces a dependency, language, or pattern the charter excludes, or ignores a convention it names, is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, and the charter line it conflicts with.

criteria.name: No obvious security faults
criteria.description: The range introduces no hard-coded secret, no string-built query or command from untrusted input, and no unsafe shell invocation.
criteria.check: Scan added lines for credentials, tokens and keys; for SQL, shell or template strings assembled from request or file input without parameterization or escaping; for shell execution with string concatenation or shell: true on user-influenced input; for disabled security defaults.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, and the category (secret, injection, unsafe shell, disabled default).

criteria.name: Every commit carries the expected Refs #N
criteria.description: Each commit in the range references the issue under review.
criteria.check: From git log <base>..<branch>, check that every commit subject or body contains Refs #N for the issue number given as input. A commit without it, or with a different issue number, is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The commit SHA and subject, and the reference it carries or lacks.

criteria.name: Declared spelling policy honored
criteria.description: User-facing text and identifiers follow the spelling policy the charter or project configuration declares, when one is declared.
criteria.check: If the charter or project configuration declares a spelling policy (for example en-GB or en-US), check added prose and identifiers against it. When no policy is declared, emit one pass finding saying so.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, the word, and the policy it breaks.

criteria.name: No debugging leftovers
criteria.description: The range leaves no debug output, breakpoints, commented-out code, or placeholder markers behind.
criteria.check: Scan added lines for console.log and print-style debug output outside logging infrastructure, debugger statements, large commented-out blocks, and TODO, FIXME, XXX or HACK markers that the issue did not ask for.
criteria.evidence: The file and line and the leftover text.

criteria.name: Failures are reported, not hidden or unhandled
criteria.description: A changed catch block, error branch or early return reports the failure it handled, rather than success, and a changed or added path that can throw or reject handles the failure rather than leaving it unhandled.
criteria.check: For each added or changed catch, error branch, early return and exit path, read what the caller receives. A finding is any path that reports success after a failure (ok: true, a success message, a repaired or done status), discards a returned { success: false } or error value without acting on it, exits 0 after a failure, or promises a warning that is never added to the warnings it returns. It is also a finding when a changed or added path can throw or reject and leaves the failure unhandled: an uncaught throw that breaks the caller's output contract (a CLI that promises a JSON result exits with a stack trace instead), or an await with no catch that leaves a busy flag, lock or dead-end state set. A missing handler counts, not only a changed one, and that the path throws rather than reporting success is not a reason to pass it.
criteria.evidence: The file and line of the error path, the failure it handles, and the success it reports instead or the result it discards; for an unhandled failure, the call that throws or rejects and what the caller is left with.

criteria.name: Edge-case input handled in changed parsing or matching
criteria.description: Changed code that parses or matches input handles the edge cases that real input carries.
criteria.check: For each added or changed parser, split, regex or comparison over text, file content, paths or JSON, ask whether it handles: CRLF line endings; git-quoted paths (spaces or non-ASCII characters, which git wraps in quotes and escapes); a JSON null, an empty value or a non-array where an array is expected; and whole-word or whole-token matching where a substring match is wrong (java inside JavaScript). An unhandled case that the input source can produce is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The file and line of the parse or match, the input case it mishandles, and what it does with that input.

criteria.name: Paths from external input stay inside their root
criteria.description: A path built from external input is checked to resolve inside the root it is meant to stay under.
criteria.check: For each added or changed path built from input this code does not control (a manifest or config file entry, renderer IPC arguments, CLI arguments, an API response), find the check that the resolved path stays inside its intended root: rejecting .. segments and absolute paths, or resolving the path and comparing it against the resolved root. A path used for a read, write, delete, spawn or network call without that check is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The file and line where the path is built, its external source, and the file-system or process operation it reaches without a containment check.

criteria.name: Writes merge into shared state rather than replacing it
criteria.description: A write to a structure that another feature or an earlier step also writes merges into it instead of replacing it whole.
criteria.check: For each added or changed write of a whole key, block, section or file (JSON written back from a partial object, a config rewritten from a fixed key list, a directory wiped before re-population, a managed block replaced), find who else writes that structure. If another feature or an earlier step writes it, a replace that drops their fields is a finding unless the range shows it reads and preserves them, or the overwrite is the stated intent.
criteria.evidence: The file and line of the write, the structure it replaces, and the other writer whose state it can drop.

criteria.name: External tool behavior is checked, not assumed
criteria.description: A call to an external CLI or API relies only on flags, output shape and executable names that the range shows were checked.
criteria.check: For each added or changed call to an external CLI or API, note what the code assumes: flags and their spelling, the output format it parses, exit codes, and the platform executable name (npm versus npm.cmd on Windows, a shell built-in versus a binary). An assumption the range does not support with a test, a recorded fixture of real output, or a cited help or documentation output is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The file and line of the call, the assumption it makes, and either the test or fixture that supports it or the statement that none is in the range.

criteria.name: A change agrees with its counterparts
criteria.description: A change made in one place is matched in the places that must agree with it.
criteria.check: For each changed function, find its counterparts and confirm they agree with the change: the sibling branches of the same conditional or switch, the reader of a value whose writer changed (and the writer of one whose reader changed), the repair step of a detection that changed, and the other call sites of a changed function or format. Use the function-context read and the same-file caller search the Read Budget already makes, and search the repository by name for a counterpart in another file. A finding is a counterpart left on the old behavior: one branch updated and its siblings not, a writer changed and its reader not, detection changed and repair not, or a value read from configuration in one place and hard-coded in another.
criteria.evidence: Both locations, as file and line: the changed site and the counterpart, and what differs between them.

criteria.name: A multi-step change cannot stop halfway or interleave
criteria.description: A change made of several steps leaves a consistent state when a step fails and when two runs overlap.
criteria.check: For each added or changed sequence of steps, ask what state is left if it stops after any one of them, and what happens if a second run starts before the first ends. A finding is: a destroy or replace that runs before its replacement has succeeded, with no rollback; a multi-file or multi-record write that is not atomic, so a failure part-way leaves some written and some not; a check-then-act on shared state (exists then create, read then write back) that another run can change in between; a stale async response that can arrive after a newer one and overwrite it; or a control or entry point left enabled while its operation runs, allowing an overlap.
criteria.evidence: The step order as file and line, and the failure point or the interleaving that leaves the inconsistent state.

criteria.name: Calls in a time-limited context are bounded
criteria.description: A synchronous or external call made where time is limited carries a timeout within the caller's own budget.
criteria.check: For each added or changed synchronous or external call (a process spawn, a network request, a file-system walk of unbounded size), find the context it runs in. When that context is time-limited (a hook, startup, a request handler or an IPC handler, or anything else the host kills or the user waits on), the call is a finding if it has no timeout, or a timeout longer than the context's own budget, so one slow call can exhaust the whole budget.
criteria.evidence: The file and line of the call, the context and its time limit, and the timeout that is missing or exceeds that limit.

findingsPolicy.perCriterion: Emit at least one finding per criterion. A criterion with no violation emits one pass finding; each violation emits its own finding at the criterion's severity.
findingsPolicy.lineAnchoring: file and line are null only for findings that are not line-anchored, such as a commit message or a whole-range observation.
findingsPolicy.describedDefect: A finding whose evidence describes a defect is warn or fail, never pass: calling it an observation, a minor note, pre-existing or outside the acceptance criteria does not make it pass. Record it at the criterion's severity and mark its age or scope with the finding's preExisting or outsideScope flag instead. A pass finding's evidence states why the code is correct, not a defect seen and set aside.

verdict.warn: Otherwise, any finding with status warn, or a non-empty budget.countedNotRead.

anti-pattern-analysis.whenMissing: Emit one pass finding with criterion anti-pattern/not-installed and continue.
